"A particular feature of KSWEB's scheduler is execution of console commands. So, KSWEB can make some work from the schedule defined by a cron expression. We suggest that a user will more often execute php scripts, because this offers great features and flexibility.

You can use the following abbreviations in the scheduler commands:
$$PHP_CGI$$ - path to the main PHP version
$$PHP_CGI_FULL$$ - path includes built-in config file
$$PHP_CLI$$ - path to PHP CLI version
$$PHP_CLI_FULL$$ - path includes built-in config file

Here are an examples of console commands that shows php script execution of the default index.php. These commands are equivalent:

Command 1: \"%1$s -f /storage/emulated/0/htdocs/index.php\"

Command 2: \"$$PHP_CGI_FULL$$ -f /storage/emulated/0/htdocs/index.php\"

You can save execution's results to a log file. Just turn this feature on in the process of job creation. Find a log file here: \"%2$s\".

If you want to execute more than one command in a job, just specify shell command script. You should enter a path to this script.

Console command: \"/storage/emulated/0/ksweb/tmp/test.sh\"

For example test.sh includes two commands:

ps
%3$s --version

Make sure the path to PHP is correct. It may change after KSWEB update. You can find more information here: Scheduler"

"The app's internal timer checks tasks every 5 seconds. Therefore, creating tasks with an interval shorter than 5 seconds is unnecessary.

Cron expressions in KSWEB are used to configure a moment of jobs executing in the scheduler. They are very similar to the cron expressions of *-nix systems. Cron expressions are composed of seven sub-expressions. These sub-expressions are separated by white-spaces. Let's examine these sub-expressions, as well as their possible values.

Seconds (0-59, allowed special Characters ', - * /')
Minutes (0-59, ', - * /')
Hours (0-23, ', - * /')
Day-of-Month (1-31, ', - * ? / L W')
Month (1-12 or JAN-DEC, ', - * /')
Day-of-Week (1-7 or SUN-SAT, ', - * ? / L #')
Year (optional field may be empty, 1970-2099, ', - * /')

You can find in the Internet information about using these special characters. Its use is similar to the cron expressions of *-nix systems.

Take a look at the examples of some KSWEB cron-like expressions:

\"0 0 12 * * ?\" - Fire at 12pm (noon) every day
\"*/10 * * * * ?\" - Fire at every 10 seconds
\"0 * 14 * * ?\" - Fire every minute starting at 2pm and ending at 2:59pm, every day
\"0 15 10 ? * - MON-FRI\" - Fire at 10:15am every Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday
\"0 15 10 ? * 6L 2002-2005\" - Fire at 10:15am on every last friday of every month during the years 2002, 2003, 2004 and 2005

To create cron expression, we suggest to use any online cron expression's generator which you will find in the Internet. Notice, that *-nix cron expressions does not contain seconds and year. So, you should add \"0\" to the first position of expression. As you saw above, \"year\" is an optional field in KSWEB cron expressions and it may still empty.

You can find more information here: Scheduler"
